ruling.explanation: Both of you agree on the underlying facts, so this comes down to arithmetic. The GPS trace and the trip record agree the completed ride was 18.0 km against a booked optimal of 10.0 km — an excess of 8.0 km. The LTA advisory (ADV-20260920-113, Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, closure 18:14–18:55) is a real event that overlaps the whole trip, and it does excuse part of that excess — but only part. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is capped at the lesser of the measured 8.0 km or 1.30 × (12.0 km shortest lawful alternative − 10.0 km booked optimal) + 1.0 km tolerance = 3.6 km. So 3.6 km is excused and 4.4 km is not. Driver: your closure argument succeeds for 3.6 km and fails for the rest. Rider: accepting the closure in chat is not a waiver of the excess the closure did not require, and the remaining 4.4 km is above the POL-RD-01 threshold measured against the adjusted route, so it stands as an unexcused deviation. The refund is then arithmetic under POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal (13.6 km, 27.2 min, since the trip record stores no amended duration). The surge multiplier of 1.00 is read from the fare breakdown, the only artifact that carries it. Recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75×13.6 + 0.28×27.2) × 1.00 + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-route ERP = 23.416. Charged total 31.42 − 23.416 = 8.004, rounded up to 8.05. That is 25.6% of the charged total, so it is a partial refund rather than a full one. On ERP: the 2.80 'Industrial loop exit' gantry is off the optimal route, and it is already comprehended inside this refund because the recomputed fare ignores it — under POL-RD-09(1) it is itemised for transparency but must not be added on top, and we have not done so. On the driver's second argument, that the rider asked for the detour: the rider's only chat message names no road or place and carries no waypoint hint, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable; this case is decided on the remaining clauses. On the driver's profile: the pre-adjustment deviation was material, so the POL-RD-06 check was run, and it is clean — deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 610 completed 90-day trips, so no repeat pattern is established, meaning no full-refund uplift and no conduct referral. On the trace: it is clean (205 fixes, 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps), so it is not impaired for policy purposes and nothing escalates. The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged (one trip ID across the records, a qualifying excess), and the rider's 60-day claim counters are zero, so no extra corroboration was required. No escalation trigger fires and no clause produces a referral.
